daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The DPR is facing mounting pressure over delays in electoral legislation as its 81st anniversary is marked. Critics have called on lawmakers to be more vocal and reduce their glamorous public appearances, while concerns grow that the electoral law revision has not been discussed despite time constraints. Observers warn that disputes and money politics could overshadow the process if the revision is rushed.

  • Former minister Muhadjir Effendy testified in court regarding the Hajj quota transfer case, revealing he had asked then-President Jokowi about the matter, and later stated that he never contacted minister Yaqut regarding the additional 10,000 quota allocation in 2022.
  • Civil society groups are urging the DPR to publish the draft Asset Forfeiture Bill for public scrutiny.
  • Minister Iskandar has called on the House to expedite the Indigenous Peoples Bill.
  • DPR Speaker Saan Mustopa defended parliamentary leadership, saying DPR officials have visited and handled drought-affected areas.
  • Fadli Zon met with President Prabowo to report public proposals for state honors.
  • Hanura party has announced a strategy to recruit new cadres through grassroots structures.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo has departed for Russia to attend the 11th Eastern Economic Forum, where he will serve as Putin's chief guest of honor. Before departing, Prabowo convened a meeting at Hambalang with the defense minister and Jakarta police chief.

  • Indonesia's Ministry of Defence has responded to reports that eight Indonesian citizens joined the Russian military, with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs also stepping in to investigate the alleged recruitment, including one individual from Depok.
  • Japan's Defense Minister is considering a visit to Indonesia on 10 September.
  • Moscow is promoting halal tourism to attract Indonesian tourists and has committed to strengthening tourism and creative economy cooperation with Jakarta.

Other

Indonesia is targeting sugar self-sufficiency and aims to end white sugar imports as part of its agricultural policy. This comes as farmers' terms of trade reached 129.19 in August 2026 according to BPS statistics.

  • Fuel prices have changed at stations across Indonesia, with some prices newly increased.
  • Garuda Indonesia has implemented new baggage regulations for passengers.
  • Indonesia has imported cattle and beef from Australia, with specific volumes now disclosed.
  • Mount Ili Lewotolok erupted again, with ash columns rising 600 meters.
  • The Forestry Minister has requested an additional Rp 4.68 trillion in budget after receiving Rp 1.55 trillion for forest fire management, opting to lease 12 aircraft rather than purchase them, with 35 foreign aircraft permits issued for Kalimantan firefighting.
  • The Ministry of Health has prepared 1,891 community health centers and 360 referral hospitals to anticipate respiratory infection cases.
